Then I learned about kintsugi: the Japanese art of repairing broken pottery with gold.

The break is not a flaw. It becomes the most valuable part.

In a world obsessed with optimization, the Japanese art of kintsugi reminds us that breakage and repair are part of history — not something to hide. T

captions.linkedin:
When your Instagram following suddenly drops by 97% overnight and all your TikToks start getting shadowbanned, what do you do? 

You roll up your sleeves, open a fresh document, and start writing. Again. 

Because here's the thing no one tells you about starting over: it's not about starting from zero. You're starting from everything you've learned so far - every mistake, every insight, every damn haiku you wrote at 3am while waiting for your follower count to tick up.

So take out a pen. Pour yourself a drink (or three). And write down the story only you can tell. Because that's how you find your way back to where you were always meant to go.

**The Art of Starting Over**🧵

The blank canvas isn’t failure—it’s freedom. We romanticize the “masterpiece” but forget the thousands of sketches thrown away to get there. Kintsun Kōri teaches us to see beauty in the broken pieces, not hide them. Your last project didn’t die; it was a lesson. A violent, beautiful lesson.
